stem: A nurse caring for a client with a Jackson-Pratt (JP) closed-suction drain is instructed to milk/strip the external tubing. What is the purpose of this technique?

options.A: Move clots through the tubing toward the collection bulb and help keep drainage flowing
options.B: Re-establish bulb suction after the collection reservoir has expanded
options.C: Prevent the drain from being accidentally pulled out of the insertion site
options.D: Measure the color and amount of drainage without opening the collection bulb

rationale: MedlinePlus guidance for a closed-suction/Jackson-Pratt drain describes stripping the drain by moving from the insertion site toward the bulb and repeating the maneuver until fluid is draining into the bulb. The same guidance notes that sudden cessation of drainage can signal a problem. Thus, when this technique is specifically instructed for a JP drain, its purpose is to move obstructing material such as clots toward the bulb and maintain drainage flow. Bulb compression, securement of the tubing, and drainage measurement are separate aspects of drain care and are not the purpose of milking/stripping the tubing.
educational_objective: Explain that prescribed milking/stripping of Jackson-Pratt tubing is used to move clots toward the bulb and maintain drainage flow, while distinguishing it from bulb suction, securement, and output measurement.
source_organization: U.S. National Library of Medicine (NLM), National Institutes of Health — MedlinePlus
source_locator: Closed suction drain with bulb > drain-stripping instructions: begin where the drain exits the body and move toward the drainage bulb; repeat until fluid drains into the bulb. 'When to Call the Doctor' includes sudden cessation of drainage as a problem requiring clinical attention.
source_claim_supported: For a Jackson-Pratt/closed-suction drain, instructed stripping of the external tubing moves obstructing material toward the bulb and helps restore/maintain drainage flow.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Physiological Adaptation, p. 14: 'Monitor and maintain devices and equipment used for drainage (e.g., surgical wound drains, chest tube suction, negative pressure wound therapy)'
blueprint_topic: Physiological Adaptation — maintenance of surgical wound drainage devices
correction_summary: Rebuilt the source item so the technique is not presented as universal for all surgical drains. Restricted the construct to a Jackson-Pratt closed-suction drain, replaced the generic NCBI Bookshelf URL with current NLM/MedlinePlus guidance and an exact locator, rewrote all distractors within the JP-drain-care construct, and corrected the blueprint from Safety and Infection Prevention and Control to Physiological Adaptation.
audit_findings: A is directly supported by current MedlinePlus JP/closed-suction drain instructions. B describes bulb-suction reactivation rather than tubing stripping; C describes securement; D describes output assessment. None is a defensible second answer. The stem avoids implying routine or universal stripping of every drain by specifying a JP drain and that the technique has been instructed. No unsupported numeric threshold or generic locator remains. Independent adversarial second pass passed.
